headline: US stocks rise as Treasury boosts long-end bond buybacks, driving yields lower amid Canada tariff pause and biotech-led gains
raw_text:
- Treasury announces plans to at least double long-end bond buybacks and expand long-dated debt repurchases, sparking a bond rally and pushing Treasury yields lower
- President Trump pauses planned 50% tariffs on Canada, further supporting risk sentiment alongside the Treasury buyback news
- Moderna (MRNA) jumps after positive Phase 3 melanoma vaccine results with Merck (MRK), marking the first success for mRNA-based cancer therapy and igniting a broad biotech rally
- BioNTech (BNTX) and Tempus AI (TEM) gain sharply in sympathy with Moderna (MRNA)’s melanoma vaccine data while Twist Bioscience (TWST) rises on separate AI-driven momentum
- Healthcare leads sector performance, with financials and industrials also firm, while technology lags and caps index upside
- Broadcom (AVGO) declines on Google-related headlines even as Marvell (MRVL) gains and Nvidia (NVDA) trades roughly flat amid reports of eased China H200 shipment restrictions
- Target (TGT) advances after a strong earnings beat and raises full-year sales and EPS guidance, helped by tariff refunds
- Lowe’s (LOW) rises despite cutting its outlook amid soft housing trends
- Estée Lauder and Pilgrim’s Pride (PPC) stand out among notable winners on stock-specific strength
- Vicor (VICR) trades lower on insider shake-up news alongside several smaller names tied to equity offerings or sector rotation, while broad tech pressure remains contained versus earlier pullbacks
